_doc: CANONICAL-CHECK declarations for financial tables whose CREATE migration is ALREADY APPLIED to production and therefore immutable (scripts/verify-applied-migrations-immutable.mjs; editing one makes db-migrate refuse to migrate and red-lines every backend pre-deploy). The declaration requirement in scripts/verify-no-duplicate-financial-ledger.mjs is not waived by this file -- it is RELOCATED. Each entry carries the same content the in-migration block would: the money concept, and an explicit naming of every colliding canonical ledger with a stated reason the new table is distinct. A declaration here is honoured ONLY when the named migration exists on disk AND actually CREATEs that table, so this file cannot declare a table into existence or cover a table it does not name.
_when_to_use: ONLY for a table whose CREATE migration was already applied before the omission was caught. A NEW table still declares INSIDE its own migration -- that is the cheaper path and it stays the default. Adding an entry here is a deliberate act with the applied timestamp recorded next to it.
_added: 2026-09-30 by Claude Lead. main was RED on verify:no-duplicate-financial-ledger for both tables below, blocking every seat's PR. Verified red by running the guard against origin/main content, not inferred from one PR.

accounting.expenses_review_queue.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.expenses_review_queue.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = NONE. accounting.expenses_review_queue is not a ledger and holds no money of its own. GRAIN: one row per AUTH-089-voided accounting.expenses row that carries no vendor_document_number, i.e. a row whose claimed duplicate cannot be confirmed from the data alone and can be resolved only by a human reading the source document. It SNAPSHOTS identifying fields (load, date, amount, memo) from the expense plus the live row AUTH-089 claimed it duplicated, so a reviewer sees both sides without re-deriving the match. CANONICAL LEDGER FOR EXPENSES REMAINS accounting.expenses -- this table never inserts, updates or voids a row there, posts no GL, carries no debit/credit, and is read by no posting path. It is a review worklist pointing AT accounting.expenses by foreign key. Removing every row in it would change no balance and no financial statement. No registry concept collides with this name (the registry has no 'expense' concept); the declaration is required because 'accounting' is a financial schema.

driver_finance.settlement_line_item_spli.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
driver_finance.settlement_line_item_spli.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = settlement line ITEM DETAIL, not settlement value. COLLIDES WITH driver_finance.driver_settlements AND WITH driver_finance.settlement_lines, and is distinct from BOTH, deliberately. driver_finance.driver_settlements remains THE canonical settlement ledger: this table creates no settlement, holds no gross/deduction/net, and never changes what a driver is paid. driver_finance.settlement_lines remains THE canonical settlement line ledger and remains the ONLY source of settlement value: this table never inserts a line, never alters a line's amount, and its rows sum to the amount of the ONE line they explain -- they redistribute nothing. GRAIN: one row per constituent item of a single pre-existing settlement_lines row that a historical AlwaysTrack import materialized as one generic extra_pay row with item_id NULL, collapsing 2-5 real document lines into one. The 17 affected lines sit in settlements 5769-5819, which are closed and verified 51/51 against AlwaysTrack and are never re-opened (owner ruling), so the item detail is recorded BESIDE the signed document rather than by editing it. Append-only, WORM-protected by 202614710000_worm_settlement_line_item_splits.sql. The permanent engine-side fix ships in the same migration: a NOT VALID check constraint on driver_finance.settlement_lines requiring item_id on every FUTURE extra_pay line, so the next import cannot recreate the defect; NOT VALID grandfathers the 17 legacy rows instead of retroactively failing closed settlements.
